mutation_targets.rationale: Removing care team constraints lets clinicians access records without membership, violating the permission matrix and care-team-gating invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_BypassCareTeam { some u: User, r: Record | u.role = ClinicianRole and (some aa: AccessAttempt | aa.user = u and aa.record = r and aa.operation = ReadRecord) and no ctm: CareTeamMembership | ctm.clinician = u and ctm.record = r and ctm.active = TRUE }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows access attempts without corresponding audit entries, violating the always-on auditing invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAuditEntry { some aa: AccessAttempt | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.accessor = aa.user and ae.operationKind = aa.operation }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the constraint allows patient or compliance officer authorship of notes, violating the append-only clinician-only invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonClinicianNote { some cn: ClinicalNote | cn.author.role != ClinicianRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the pairing between patient role and assigned record lets patients access multiple records or have no assigned record, violating ownership invariants.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_BrokenPatientOwnership { some p: User | p.role = PatientRole and (no r: Record | p.assignedRecordId = r) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing permission rules lets roles bypass their restrictions; e.g., compliance officer reads clinical content.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionBypass { some u: User | u.role = ComplianceOfficerRole and (u -> ReadRecord) in PermissionMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit structure constraint lets accessor snapshots diverge from actual role, violating attribution correctness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongSnapshot { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.accessorRoleSnapshot != ae.accessor.role }
